cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: See What This Took
cards.instruction: Make someone recognize the courage, restraint, or emotional labor your choices required.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've sealed the angry letter in this envelope. Hold it beside the apology I sent you. Feel the difference.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I appreciate the apology. I don't need the angry version.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Just hold it a moment. Writing sorry took ten minutes; not sending those six pages took all night.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Six pages? Now I want to open it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep it shut. You can weigh it in your hand; I want credit for not saying those things.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 directs a comparison; A3 reduces participation to holding so B recognizes the restraint; A5 permits weighing but not opening to preserve cooperation and the achievement.

responseLogic.evidence: A1 explicitly seals the angry letter; B4 wants to open it and A5 keeps it shut, so no unseen folding or reading is needed.

relationship.evidence: B2 accepts the apology without wanting anger; B4 six pages makes curiosity an immediate competing desire.

heightening.evidence: B4 opening would expose what A withheld; A5 adapts the demonstration to weight alone while seeking credit.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes sealed angry version and sent apology addressed to B; A3 states the effort of withholding it.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 prohibition, permitted substitute and recognition request each change what B should do or acknowledge; the demand for credit is deliberately plain.
